goal: Wire the harness BLOCKED branch to validate requires against the task and persist them on the lifecycle, and add a public recheck_blocked_lifecycle primitive that re-evaluates the predicates and applies the INTERRUPTED -> READY transition with new harness.recheck_attempted / harness.unblocked events.

references: src/flywheel/harness.py:665-690 -- current Intent.BLOCKED branch; extend it to (a) reject envelopes whose command_grader predicates do not resolve in task.graders (via the existing harness.protocol_failure path), (b) JSON-serialize the requires tuple onto lifecycle.blocked_requires_json before the -> INTERRUPTED transition, and (c) put the serialized payload into the existing harness.blocked event payload alongside reason
src/flywheel/harness.py:785-810 -- existing protocol-failure path that the new task-aware rejection routes through; reuse _envelope_protocol_error / _finalize_attempt / _transition wiring
src/flywheel/harness.py:462-466 -- run_task entry-time normalization that drains INTERRUPTED -> READY; this must continue to work for SIGINT-paused lifecycles where blocked_requires_json IS NULL

src/flywheel/lifecycle.py:100-126 -- Lifecycle.transition_to; centralize blocked_requires_json clearing here when target == Status.READY (any caller, any retry edge, any normalization) so we cannot forget a code path

src/flywheel/grader_command.py -- reuse the existing CommandGrader runner for command_grader predicate evaluation; the recheck path must NOT write to grader_results (per spec FR-5, recheck is a control-plane operation)
constraints: BLOCKED branch in _run_attempt: after parse_envelope returns ValidEnvelope(intent=BLOCKED, ...), validate every CommandGraderRequirement.name against task.graders. A name absent from task.graders, or present but referring to a non-command grader, is a protocol failure: route through the existing harness.protocol_failure path (emit the event, finalize attempt as Outcome.AGENT_ERROR, transition VALIDATING-or-RUNNING -> FAILED_VALIDATION using the same code path the parse-time protocol failures use). Do NOT emit harness.blocked in this case.

On the happy BLOCKED path: serialize the envelope.requires tuple to a stable JSON string (each predicate as {type, ...fields}; order preserved) and set lifecycle.blocked_requires_json before the transition to INTERRUPTED. The harness.blocked event payload gains a 'requires' key with the same structured list (alongside the existing reason).

Add Lifecycle.transition_to: when target == Status.READY, set self.blocked_requires_json = None. This is the single chokepoint that covers recheck, FAILED_VALIDATION -> READY retries, INTERNAL_ERROR -> READY retries, and run_task entry-time normalization of INTERRUPTED lifecycles. flywheel.lifecycle must stay pure (no json import).
Add a public dataclass `RecheckOutcome(applied: bool, reason: str, per_predicate: tuple[dict[str, object], ...])` in flywheel.harness. Export it from flywheel.harness.__all__.

Add public function `recheck_blocked_lifecycle(store: HarnessStore, run_id: str, task: Task, *, now: Callable[[], datetime] | None = None) -> RecheckOutcome`. Behavior per spec FR-5: (a) load lifecycle; if status != INTERRUPTED or blocked_requires_json is None, return RecheckOutcome(applied=False, reason='not_blocked', per_predicate=()) with NO events emitted; (b) parse the persisted requires JSON back into the BlockedRequirement tuple; (c) evaluate each predicate against worker CWD and process env -- command_grader resolves the named grader from task.graders and runs it via the existing command-grader runner WITHOUT writing a grader_results row; file_exists uses os.path.exists; env_var_set checks os.environ.get(name) for a non-empty value; (d) emit harness.recheck_attempted with payload {per_predicate: [{type, identifier, satisfied, detail}, ...], all_satisfied: bool}; (e) if all satisfied, transition INTERRUPTED -> READY (which clears blocked_requires_json via the centralized clearer), emit harness.unblocked with payload {from_status: 'interrupted', to_status: 'ready'}, and return RecheckOutcome(applied=True, ...); (f) otherwise return RecheckOutcome(applied=False, ...) with no transition.

Add a `recheck_dry_run_blocked_lifecycle` variant (or a `dry_run: bool = False` kwarg on recheck_blocked_lifecycle -- author's choice, but document the chosen shape) that performs the predicate evaluation and emits harness.recheck_attempted but skips the harness.unblocked emission and the -> READY transition. The CLI task depends on this primitive, so it must exist now.

Add a new file tests/test_harness_recheck.py covering, with both InMemoryStore and SqliteStore via parametrization where reasonable: (a) all-satisfied path transitions INTERRUPTED -> READY, clears blocked_requires_json, emits both events; (b) any-unsatisfied path emits only harness.recheck_attempted, no transition, blocked_requires_json preserved; (c) non-INTERRUPTED lifecycle is a silent no-op (no events); (d) INTERRUPTED with blocked_requires_json IS NULL (the SIGINT-pause case) is a silent no-op; (e) command_grader predicate re-runs the named grader (exit code surfaced in detail); (f) command_grader predicate referencing a grader name no longer on the task evaluates as satisfied=false with detail='grader not found', no transition; (g) dry-run path emits recheck_attempted only, no transition, no harness.unblocked; (h) command_grader does NOT write a grader_results row.

Extend tests/test_harness.py: (a) BLOCKED happy path now asserts lifecycle.blocked_requires_json is set and the harness.blocked payload carries the structured list; (b) BLOCKED with an unknown command_grader name routes through harness.protocol_failure and ends in FAILED_VALIDATION (no harness.blocked emitted); (c) any existing test that constructed ValidEnvelope(intent=Intent.BLOCKED, ...) without `requires` (see tests/test_harness.py:475 and :852) must be updated to include a valid requires tuple -- the envelope-level change in the prerequisite task already enforces this, so these tests will be red until you fix them.

Update docs/task-lifecycle.md to note that INTERRUPTED -> READY can be driven by recheck_blocked_lifecycle (in addition to SIGINT-pause normalization and manual operator promotion). One-or-two-sentence addition only.
Run `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` on every .py file you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting verify.
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (e.g. 'feat:') before reporting verify.
non_goals: Do not add the `flywheel recheck-blocked` CLI subcommand or extend `flywheel status` in this task -- both belong to the next task in the phase.
Do not add a manual_ack predicate type or any new predicate type beyond the three already defined in the envelope task.

Do not auto-recheck inside run_task entry-time normalization. Recheck remains explicit-only per spec Decisions Log; the existing INTERRUPTED -> READY drain stays for SIGINT-pause resumes (which have blocked_requires_json IS NULL).
Do not persist recheck command-grader results into the grader_results table -- the recheck event payload is the audit surface (spec Out of Scope).
Do not recreate or re-enter the original attempt's sandbox at recheck time -- caller is responsible for the CWD (spec Out of Scope).
edge_cases: An INTERRUPTED lifecycle whose serialized requires JSON is unparseable (data corruption) must surface as a RecheckOutcome(applied=False) with a descriptive reason and an emitted harness.recheck_attempted whose payload notes the parse failure -- do not crash the caller.

Two concurrent recheck callers on the same lifecycle: optimistic concurrency on lifecycle.version (existing semantics) decides the winner; the loser surfaces StoreConcurrencyError to its caller -- do not swallow it.
command_grader predicate subprocess fails to start (e.g. binary missing): predicate is unsatisfied; detail string includes the OS error; no exception escapes the recheck function.
env_var_set where the variable is set to the empty string: predicate is unsatisfied (spec FR-2 non-empty rule).
file_exists.present=false and the path exists: predicate is unsatisfied.
Recheck called on a DONE / FAILED / PENDING / READY lifecycle: silent no-op (status != INTERRUPTED branch).
